title: Preview a page of components and use it: hover, press, toggle and focus show each component's own looks
goal: A person who has made a page of components (buttons, switches, fields, tabs, each with looks for its states) has no way to try it: the canvas is always for editing, so they cannot hover a button to see its Hover look or click a switch to see it turn On. Add a Preview mode for the page in front of them, where every component behaves like the real control, using only the looks they made, with nothing to set up.
notes: User, 2026-11-04 (intake): 'When we make a component, i'm not sure how to preview it interactively. e.g. i make a page with a bunch of components and want to preview it and hover over things or click on things...is this possible already?' and 2026-11-05: 'what happened to previewing the states of controls' (the intake window had proposed Preview mode and not filed it). Today: components have looks per state (ComponentVersionMatching names them), nothing plays them. Objective ui-prototyping ('Click-through prototyping') was staged later; this is its first step, asked for by the user. Mock reference: docs/design/mocks/pages/ui-prototype.html.
acceptance: DESIGN FIRST, as an interactive mock on the design site (like pages/selection-transform.html): how Preview is entered (a Preview button in the title bar and a shortcut, Command-Return proposed) and left (Escape, the same button); what the window looks like in Preview (editing chrome gone, the page at 100 percent or fitted, a small Preview pill saying how to leave); what each kind of component does. Show it to the user as a decision card with the mock link and a marked screenshot, and build after approval.

In Preview, at Next defaults: pointing at a component shows its Hover look; pressing shows Pressed; releasing over it is a click. A click on a switch, checkbox, radio, tab or segmented control flips it to its On or Selected look and it stays (a radio or tab group keeps one selected); Tab and Shift-Tab move Focus with the Focused look; a component shown in its Disabled look does not respond. A component with no look for a state simply keeps its current look for that state.

Which look means which state comes from the look's own name and kind, as the component sheets already name them (Default, Hover, Pressed, Focused, Disabled, On, Off, Selected), not from anything set by hand; a component whose looks are named otherwise gets a short note in Preview, not an error.
Nothing in Preview changes the document: leaving puts every component back as it was, and Undo history is untouched.

Walks: enter Preview on a page with a button, a switch, a tab group and a disabled field; hover, press, click, Tab; leave and confirm the document is unchanged. A reel in the audit under queue/audits/.

The later step (connections between frames, click a button to go to another page, as docs/design/mocks/pages/ui-prototype.html draws) is NOT part of this task; note it in the log for the user to ask for.
Anything left rough is filed as a follow-up task if it clears the follow-up bar (queue/bin/follow-up-bar.md), and written into this task's log if it does not.

Design done, no app code touched: docs/design/mocks/pages/component-preview.html, interactive, in the design site's nav under Prototyping. Its engine is the rule a build would run, in miniature; its word lists are AgentComponentSense's. Card preview-a-page-of-components-and-use-it-hover-pr-should-a-page-of-components-work has two marked pictures and a brief.

Checked in the browser with trusted clicks, hovers and keys on the Preview button, Save, the switch, a tab, a segment word, Tab, Esc and Cmd-Return, plus dispatched pointer events through the page's own handlers for press, slide off, slide back and release off. Hover, Pressed, click, flip, one tab kept, Month picked, Focused all read right; document JSON identical after leaving; Undo count 14 throughout; Show me ran to the end with no console errors. This proves the prototype's rules, not the app: nothing is built.

Adversarial review of the design, found by running it: (1) Ask leaving moved the Preview button about 97 pt under the pointer, so the second click missed: Ask now keeps its space. (2) A held press lit Hover on other controls: fixed. (3) The panel only went invisible, keeping 268 pt, since .edit.lean is flex, not grid: now collapses. (4) In a short window the pill sat 54 pt over the page: fit leaves its strip and the page is centred by hand; measured 8 pt clear at 520 and 420 high. (5) A plain Hover on an On or Selected copy would flip it back: a latched look needs a look naming both, else it stays. (6) Real sheets draw a segmented control as ONE component with looks named for its words, which state names alone miss: a click on the word shows that look. (7) A first timer cannot tell what is live; left as is, since a hint would add chrome and Preview draws only their looks. The user can say if it stalls them.

Chose a Preview button over reusing View and Edit because View already means a player on a video; the card offers the switch as option b. Chose Cmd-Return because no menu row holds it, the text field's use only applies while it has the keyboard, and ui-prototype.html prints it for Play flow; neither Photoshop nor Premiere settles it (UX-PATTERNS §7). Chose same parent as the rule for one group over nearness because the document already holds it. Chose Tab stopping only where a Focused look can show over a ring of our own because the task says only the looks they made. Chose instant look changes over a crossfade to match real Mac controls.

For the build, after approval. Pure core first, test first: state words beside AgentComponentSense, shown look, click, tab stops. Each variant question is read on its own, so a Type x State x Size copy only changes its State answer and nearestComponentDrawing covers the rest. Draw through displayDocument with the swapped instanceVersion on a throwaway value, never History.perform. Still to settle while building: a document changed from outside during Preview (an agent's tool call) should rebuild the throwaway copy; whether measurements hide; a long component name in the pill note must stay inside the 30 character chrome budget; main drawings on a sheet rest on their own look, so the Hover column shows Hover at rest.
Left for the user to ask for, per the checklist: connections between frames, click a button to go to another page, as ui-prototype.html draws. Also not in this step: typing into a field.
